question: Rectangle \(ABCD\) has \(AB=3\) and \(BC=4.\) Point \(E\) is the foot of the perpendicular from \(B\) to diagonal \(\overline{AC}.\) What is the area of \(\triangle ADE?\)
solution:
Compare \(\triangle ADE\) with \(\triangle ABE\), since the perpendicular \(BE\) makes the latter a right triangle.

Both \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle ADC\) have area
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot4=6.
\]
They share base \(AC\), so \(B\) and \(D\) have equal perpendicular distances from line \(AC\). Therefore \(\triangle ABE\) and \(\triangle ADE\), which share base \(AE\) on that line, also have equal areas.

By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
AC=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5.
\]
Triangles \(ABE\) and \(ACB\) are similar: \(\angle AEB=\angle ABC=90^\circ\), and \(\angle BAE=\angle CAB\) because \(E\) lies on \(AC\). Their corresponding hypotenuses are \(AB=3\) and \(AC=5\), so their area ratio is
\[
\left(\frac35\right)^2=\frac9{25}.
\]
Since \(\triangle ACB\) has area \(6\),
\[
\operatorname{Area}(ADE)=\operatorname{Area}(ABE)
=\frac9{25}\cdot6=\frac{54}{25}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{54}{25}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
